input.brief: Joshua Ogallo, Nairobi frontend software engineer and digital creative with two separate portfolios, real enterprise systems and agency brand work, an immersive original sculptural JO monogram using only free assets

direction.name: The name as a monument
direction.idea: The name is the headline. Set it so large that it becomes architecture: as wide as the viewport, cropped by an edge, or stacked to fill the screen. Nothing else on the first screen competes; the description of what this is drops to a single small sentence. The idea comes from treating the name's letters as material. Ask what the subject can do to its own name: a photograph of the work sits inside a counter or replaces a letter, the name repeats down the page like a reel, the letters are split to opposite corners and the page happens between them. In the study this was the single most common device among sites scoring 7.5 or more.
direction.composition: First screen: the wordmark spans 88–100% of the viewport width (font-size 16–24vw, set with a clamp so it never wraps), anchored either to the bottom edge with its descenders nearly touching it, or dead centre with everything else pushed to the corners. One line of supporting text at 16–20px sits in a corner on a shared margin; navigation is three or four words in the opposite corner. After the hero the page is deliberately small and calm: a narrow text column or a simple two-column grid, so the contrast with the monument holds. The name returns once more at full width as the footer, in the inverse colours. Margins are tight (20–32px) so the type reaches the edges. Two type sizes do nearly all the work: the monument and a small text size, with one mid size for section headings.
direction.typography: One family. The display cut must survive enormous sizes: tight tracking (-0.04 to -0.07em), leading 0.8–0.9, optical kerning on. Section headings are modest (28–40px) on purpose.
direction.colour: Two values carry the page (ground and ink). The accent, if used at all, appears on one thing only: the single action or the inset image frame. The footer inverts ground and ink.
direction.imagery: Few images, used as inserts in the typography rather than as illustrations beside it: one photograph inside or behind the name (a 4:5 or 1:1 frame replacing a letter, or tucked between two words), then a short run of large full-width or half-width photographs further down. Square corners. No collage of small thumbnails.
direction.richness: Scale. The size of the name against the smallness of everything else is the entire visual event, so protect both ends: do not shrink the name to make room, and do not let body text creep above 20px.
direction.pitfalls: A long name set small is just a logo. If the name has more than about 12 characters, stack it on two lines or crop it with the viewport edge; never drop below 12vw. Do not add a second big headline under the name. Do not decorate the letters.

hero.name: Film title, bottom edge
hero.blueprint: One photograph fills the viewport at 100vw by 100svh, `object-fit: cover`, with its subject in the upper two-thirds and a calmer, darker zone along the bottom. The name is one condensed uppercase word, or a short name in a high-contrast serif, set at clamp(150px, 17.5vw, 290px) and sized to span the full width between 32px margins. It is centred and anchored so its baseline sits 34px above the bottom edge, covering roughly the lowest quarter of the frame. A soft neutral dark scrim lies under that bottom band only, about 40% of the height; the rest of the image is untouched. Directly above the name's left end, on the same margin, sits the supporting sentence at 16px on two short lines. Directly above its right end, right-aligned, sits the single action as a small paper-coloured rectangular button. The top edge carries a small emblem or wordmark at the left margin and up to five text links at 15px grouped at the right, all in white. The central half of the screen belongs to the view.
hero.mobile: The photograph is re-cropped to portrait with `object-position` on its subject and fills 100svh. The name stays on the bottom edge at 22vw on one line, or two lines at 20vw beyond eight characters, 20px above the edge. The supporting sentence sits above the name's left end at 15px. The action button moves to the top-right corner and the links collapse to a menu word beside the emblem.
hero.headline: The name of the place: one word of up to about 12 characters at 17.5vw, or two words stacked on a phone.

photos.title: Architecture
photos.note: structure, lines, bridges, facades and building interiors

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Giant title, uneven wall
sections.blueprint: A one- or two-word title in capitals at clamp(72px, 9vw, 136px), leading 0.9, sits flush left at the 16px margin; on its baseline at the far right, one underlined link at 15px to the full archive. 32px below, thumbnails pack into an uneven wall with 8px gaps: a flex-wrap layout in which each row has a different fixed height (cycle 240, 360, 200, 300px) and each tile's width follows its image ratio, so widths range from one-sixth to one-half of the page and tile edges do not line up between rows. Rows are justified to both margins with `flex-grow`. Under each image, one caption line at 12px: project name left, year in the soft ink right. Square corners; no hover overlay beyond a slight dimming of the other tiles. Holds 9–16 projects. The section ground is one flat colour, dark or saturated, edge to edge.
sections.mobile: Title at 17vw on one line. The wall becomes rows of alternating composition: one full-width tile, then two tiles splitting the width 62/38, then 38/62, with 6px gaps and fixed row heights of 220 and 150px. Captions stay as one line under each tile.

sections.name: Side facts, wide paragraph
sections.blueprint: Two rows share one vertical line at 34% of the viewport width. Row one: in a 160px column at the left margin, three label and value pairs stack with 20px between them, each a label in the soft ink with its value beneath in full ink, all at 13px (founded, based in, team size). From the 34% line a five-line paragraph at clamp(20px, 1.7vw, 26px), leading 1.35, runs to 90% of the width. Row two starts 120px lower and repeats the logic for the record of the practice: one plain word at 13px at the far left (awards, press, clients), then from the 34% line two list columns, each 260px wide with a 64px gutter, at 13px with 10px between lines: name at the left, year at the right in the soft ink. No heading; the paragraph opens the section. Each list comfortably holds 6–12 lines. No photographs are needed.
sections.mobile: Everything aligns to the left margin. The paragraph comes first at 19px. The three label and value pairs follow as a two-column grid at 14px. The two record lists stack with 40px between them, each opened by its plain word in full ink.

sections.name: Address in display rows
sections.blueprint: The contact block is a stack of five full-width rows, every one set at the same size, clamp(44px, 6vw, 88px), regular weight, left-aligned with a 20px inset and leading 1.0: the building or venue name, the street, the city with postcode, the opening hours as one compact line, the phone number. Each row is about 150px tall with the text sitting in its lower third; rows are told apart by alternating two flat tones of the section colour as full-width bands, or by 28px of space alone. A sixth row holds a one-word greeting at the same size followed, 24px to its right and centred on the x-height, by a solid round button 0.9em across with an arrow, which opens the email or booking link. Street and phone rows are links (map, call). No heading and no form. Optionally, one small round photograph sits at the right end of the first row.
sections.mobile: Rows at 9.6vw with 16px insets, about 84px tall; the hours break onto two rows (days, then times). The greeting row becomes a full-width band in the accent colour with the round arrow button at its right end, 56px across.

references.name: Nia Creative
references.idea: The three-letter wordmark becomes a slot-machine reel: the name repeats vertically and its middle letter is swapped for a square of client photography or video.
references.hero: Pale grey field with a slim nav: bracketed lowercase logo top-left, four uppercase mono links centred, a black pill button top-right. The centre 43% of the width holds a vertical reel of the wordmark stacked three times in very heavy black grotesk, each row about 230px tall; in every row the middle letter is replaced by a square photo or video tile (surfers, a woman holding glasses over her eyes, a burger). The middle row is sharp; rows above and below fade out through gradient masks. A bottom strip carries a mono descriptor at left and city plus live clock at right. A plum band starts at the fold.
references.type: A heavy, tightly tracked grotesk (xgnl) carries the wordmark, a 70px lowercase section word and bold 20 to 34px statements; body is the same face at 14px, bold. Geist Mono in small capitals handles nav, categories, bracketed indexes and the clock.
references.colour: #f3f3f3 #574d56 #515144 #1c1c1c #b9aebd #b3b586 — Pale grey base with black type. Two muted full-width bands, dusty plum and olive, set their text in a lighter tint of the band colour rather than white. Photography supplies the saturation.
references.imagery: Flash-lit hospitality and lifestyle photography plus short video: cocktails, hotel rooms, food, trail runners. Portrait tiles with one or two large rounded corners, square tiles inside the wordmark, and an edge-to-edge three-up strip.
references.layout: 28px side margins and a three-column grid for work. Big lowercase section words sit flush left with a small paragraph flush right. Sections alternate pale grey grids, coloured statement bands and full-bleed image strips; a black rounded nav bar pins to the top after the hero.

sections.description: Dusty plum band about one viewport tall. A bold 34px statement in pale lilac sits top-left across half the width, one phrase underlined with a hand-drawn stroke. Lower left, a small heading and eight industries in tiny uppercase mono split into two bulleted columns. At the right margin a tall portrait photo, about 20% of the width, with large rounded corners, overlaps the band's top edge and leaves the middle of the band empty.

A 70px heavy lowercase word flush left with a three-line 14px paragraph flush right on the same baseline. Below, three equal columns with wide gutters: each has a portrait image narrower than its column with a large radius on the bottom-right corner only, then a 20px project name, a mono uppercase category and a four-line bold description. Rows repeat with no dividers or card backgrounds.

Three photographs or clips butt together edge to edge with no gaps, each a third of the viewport wide and about 40% of a screen tall. Immediately below, an olive band: a three-line 26px statement in pale olive at left with one underlined phrase, two lines of small copy beneath it, and a small rounded portrait image tucked into the lower right corner.

Services as stacked sheets. Each is a full-width panel with a 1px outline and large top-corner radius that slides up over the previous one. The left half is empty except for a centred column: a bracketed mono index, a 26px bold title and four centred lines of sub-services. The right half is one photograph with rounded corners filling the panel height.

steal: Drop a photo tile into the wordmark in place of one letter and run the lockup as a vertical reel with masked top and bottom rows.
On coloured bands, set type in a lighter tint of the band's own hue instead of white to keep the band calm.
Round only one corner of each image tile, the same corner every time, as a quiet signature shape.

references.name: Produx Design
references.idea: The wordmark is the hero, and the showreel image assembles itself from scattered square fragments as you scroll.
references.hero: Near-black field with 80px side margins. The wordmark, in a wide, light-weight uppercase sans with a slashed O, runs margin to margin (about 89% of the width) with a cap height near 20% of the viewport, starting 9% from the top. A large empty gap follows. In the lower half a two-line statement at 5.1vw sits flush left; opposite it, bottom-aligned to the statement and flush to the right margin, is a three-line paragraph in small monospace about a quarter of the width. No nav bar, button or image in the first viewport; the bottom quarter is empty.
references.type: At Aero in light-to-medium weight for the wordmark, the 74px statement and project titles; DM Mono for the hero paragraph, bracketed nav items and uppercase project blurbs at about 11px. Three sizes; the statement is roughly five times the mono text.
references.colour: #0e0e0e #e4e4e4 #545e54 #303930 #6f8f3a — Near-black page with off-white type and no accent colour. Colour arrives only through imagery: moss green and sage in the showreel render, then each case-study thumbnail brings its own palette.
references.imagery: A 3D render of a moss-covered boulder on a sage background, first broken into scattered square tiles, then whole as a 16:9 inset. Work thumbnails are square-cornered stills and video in mixed ratios, including one vivid orange-violet gradient card.
references.layout: 80px margins. After the hero, a small logo top-left and four bracketed mono links spread across the right half. Hero is all type, the next three screens are a pinned image assembly, then a work grid with unequal column widths and mono captions under each thumbnail.

sections.description: Pinned showreel reveal on black. Eight to ten small square tiles, 60 to 100px, each a different crop of the same image, float scattered around the centre at different depths, some blurred. As scroll advances they multiply, enlarge and lock together until they form one 16:9 image inset at about 70% of viewport width, with the wordmark centred on it in white and tiny captions overlaid at left and lower right.

Two unequal columns on black, roughly 52% and 30% of the width with a wide gutter. Each item is a square-cornered thumbnail with a row of small rectangular mono tags along its bottom edge; beneath it a small square bullet, the project name in the sans at about 16px and a two-line uppercase mono blurb. The next item breaks the grid: a single thumbnail centred at about 75% width.

steal: Run the wordmark margin to margin in a light weight rather than a heavy one; thin strokes at huge size read as assured instead of loud.
Pair one large sans statement with a tiny monospace paragraph bottom-aligned on the opposite margin and leave the middle of the row empty.
Introduce the hero image as scattered square crops of itself that converge into the full frame on scroll.
references.media: The fold has no media at all; the first picture is the 40s showreel, which arrives on the second screen as scattered square tiles at different depths that converge into an inset 16:9 frame, then fills 56-96% of each screen until it is full-bleed at about 4850px. Below: a staggered two-column mosaic with a centred wide interlude, a logo strip bleeding off both edges, and a pinned 3D stone centre-right with the statement docked bottom-left; zero radius everywhere.
references.motion: Black at 400ms, then wordmark letters rise one by one out of a baseline mask, tagline words rise in masked lines and the small blurb types itself out, settled by about 2.2s. Lenis drives a sticky, scrubbed hero in which tiles fly in from depth, blurred to sharp, assemble the frame and scale it to full bleed, then headings resolve through a pixel-slice glitch, work frames reveal by inset clip, the manifesto colours word by word and the closing stone grows moss as the ground turns from black to moss green, all as per-frame script (44,246 style mutations) with no GSAP exposed.

references.name: Artem Shcherbakov
references.idea: A director's reel hides behind a small pill-shaped window that scrolls open to fill the screen, while neon-green marker scribbles deface the polite typography.
references.hero: White page. Three nav words are pinned to the very top: one hard left, the name centred, one hard right, in bold condensed lowercase about 28px, touching the edges. The content is a single horizontal row at mid-height in three equal parts. Left: a two-line greeting in an ultra-heavy rounded sans at about 6vw, with a neon-green hand-scrawled word and underline drawn over it. Centre: a vertical rounded-rectangle window about 180 by 300px showing zoomed, pixelated video. Right: a green doodle face above a centred six-line bio at about 22px. A tiny grey scroll cue sits bottom-centre. More than 60% is white.
references.type: EaseDouble at weight 900 with -0.08em tracking, letters nearly fused, for display; plain Arial Narrow for nav and body, bold in the nav. About 88px display against roughly 22px body. Display type melts into soft blobs between states.
references.colour: #ffffff #0e0e0e #17e84a #ff2ecb — Black on white, inverting to white on near-black for the footer. One neon green is reserved for hand-drawn scribbles and doodles, with a single touch of magenta.
references.imagery: CG character footage treated with scanlines, colour fringing and heavy pixelation, shown first inside a small pill mask and then full-bleed. Crude marker doodles (faces, robot, clapperboard) in green outline are scattered around it.
references.layout: A short single-scroll sequence: three-part intro row, full-bleed video with a stacked project list, a centred paragraph in display type, a dark contact panel. Nav words stay in the top corners throughout. No grid lines, no cards, no section headings.

sections.description: The video fills the viewport edge to edge. Project names are stacked bottom-left in the heavy rounded face at about 5vw, lowercase with tight leading, in translucent white so footage shows through; the active name turns solid white and gets a green scribble across it. The list runs off the bottom edge. In a later state the video shrinks to a rounded rectangle about two-thirds of the viewport wide.

A centred five-line paragraph set entirely in the 900-weight rounded display face at about 4.5vw on white, tracked so tightly the letters touch. The last line is caught mid-reveal as soft black blobs, showing that each line condenses from a blurred, gooey state into legible type.

Near-black panel. A two-line centred heading in white display type sits at the top with green and magenta scribbles over a few letters. Below, a narrow centred column lists contact details in small plain sans, each preceded by a tiny grey label. Five or six green line doodles are scattered around the edges, some cropped by the viewport.

steal: Start the showreel as a small pill-shaped mask in the hero and let scrolling grow it to full-bleed.
Overdraw clean display type with a single-colour hand scribble to add personality without a second typeface.
Pair one extravagant display face with a deliberately default system face (Arial Narrow) for everything functional.
references.media: The first screen is white type with almost no picture. From the first scroll step a project reel drawn into a WebGL canvas with a scanline and colour-fringe shader covers the whole screen behind a giant credit list, then shrinks to a centred rounded card of about 720x880, and later a black pill rises and grows into a full dark panel ringed by green line doodles, all without a video element in the DOM.
references.motion: A tiny percentage counter runs about 4.5s, stalling at 54 for over a second, then the nav and role line sharpen from blur (filter .7s, opacity 1.2s, cubic-bezier(.33,1,.68,1)). Custom smooth scroll pins the footage while the credit list rises over it, the frame contracts into a card, manifesto words go from blur to sharp in scroll order, and a pill expands by clip-path into the contact panel; display type melts through a goo threshold before it sets.
